ideas.pitch: An offline, rule-based static analysis and root-cause visualizer for complex pseudo-code and game systems.
ideas.problem_statement: Round 1 & Round 2: Pseudo-code debugging and game file functional bug fixing under time pressure.
ideas.title: DebugPulse
ideas.why_it_could_win: Targeting the specific diagnostic and systems thinking requirements of GDA CRCE's competitive debugging format without relying on banned external AI tools for Round 1.

ideas.pitch: A dependency graph visualizer designed to expose cascading state corruption across interconnected game systems.
ideas.problem_statement: Final Round: A complex final project containing interconnected systems and cascading bugs.
ideas.title: CascadeTrace
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly tackles the final round's hardest challenge—tracing cascading bugs across deeply coupled architecture—appealing directly to judges testing practical fixability.

ideas.pitch: A lightweight diagnostic dashboard for rapid asset state inspection and memory tracking in game debugging.
ideas.problem_statement: Round 2: Project/game files containing functional bugs to locate and fix.
ideas.title: GlitchLens
ideas.why_it_could_win: Maximizes diagnostic speed during Round 2 by giving the team an intuitive telemetry dashboard tailored to typical game loop failures.

ideas.pitch: A local practice harness for multi-file pseudo-code logic tracing and syntax validation.
ideas.problem_statement: Round 1: Pseudo-code debugging involving multiple problem statements, game visuals, and pseudo-code.
ideas.title: PseudoDrill
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses the exact constraint of Round 1 where internet access is permitted but AI tools are strictly banned, providing internal verification logic.

ideas.pitch: A state-rollback and event-sourcing recorder for tracking asynchronous game loop exceptions during stress tests.
ideas.problem_statement: Final Round: A complex final project containing interconnected systems and cascading bugs.
ideas.title: StateReplay
ideas.why_it_could_win: Solves the exact difficulty of late-stage debugging by allowing judges and competitors to step backwards through execution timelines.
